questions.question:
The marks obtained by the students of a class are given. Find the standard deviation of the marks (rounded off to 2 decimal places).

 65, 47, 59, 75, 82, 91, 55 and 78
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marks obtained: 65, 47, 59, 75, 82, 91, 55, 78

**Formula used:**

Standard deviation (σ) = sqrt{dfrac{sum (x_i - mu)²}{n}}

Where: μ = Mean, xᵢ = Individual values, n = Number of values

**Calculations:**

μ = dfrac{65+47+59+75+82+91+55+78}{8}

⇒ μ = dfrac{552}{8} = 69

Deviation (xi - μ) and square of deviation

(65 - 69)² = (-4)² = 16

(47 - 69)² = (-22)² = 484

(59 - 69)² = (-10)² = 100

(75 - 69)² = (6)² = 36

(82 - 69)² = (13)² = 169

(91 - 69)² = (22)² = 484

(55 - 69)² = (-14)² = 196

(78 - 69)² = (9)² = 81

Sum of squared deviations

sum (x - bar{x})² = 16 + 484 + 100 + 36 + 169 + 484 + 196 + 81 = 1566

Variance σ² = frac{sum (x - bar{x})²}{N} = (1566)/(8) = 195.75

Standard Deviation σ = sqrt{195.75}

⇒ σ ≈ 13.991068... ≈ 13.99

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question:
If the mode of the following data is 165, then what is the value of x?

 
 

 Class
 150-155
 155-160
 160-165
 165-170
 170-175
 
 
 
 

 Frequency
 13
 26
 37
 x
 27
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Class intervals: 150-155, 155-160, 160-165, 165-170, 170-175

Frequencies: 13, 26, 37, x, 27

Mode = 165

**Formula used:**

Mode = L + [(fₘ - f₁) / (2fₘ - f₁ - f₂)] × h

Where:

 
• L = lower boundary of modal class
 
• fₘ = frequency of modal class
 
• f₁ = frequency of class preceding modal class
 
• f₂ = frequency of class succeeding modal class
 
• h = class width

**Calculation:**

Modal class = 165-170 (since Mode = 165, and 165 is in this class).

L = 165, fₘ = x, f₁ = 37, f₂ = 27, h = 5

Substitute values into the formula:

165 = 165 + [(x - 37) / (2x - 37 - 27)] × 5

⇒ 165 - 165 = [(x - 37) / (2x - 64)] × 5

⇒ 0 = [(x - 37) / (2x - 64)] × 5

⇒ (x - 37) = 0

⇒ x = 37

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: If the mode of a data set exceeds its mean by 37.8, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode − Mean = 37.8

**Formula used:**

Empirical formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

**Calculations:**

Let Mean = M

⇒ Mode = M + 37.8

Now use formula:

M + 37.8 = 3 × Median − 2M

⇒ 3 × Median = M + 37.8 + 2M = 3M + 37.8

⇒ Median = (3M + 37.8) ÷ 3 = M + 12.6

⇒ Mode − Median = (M + 37.8) − (M + 12.6) = 25.2

**∴ Mode exceeds the median by 25.2**

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 20.1, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula)

questions.question: If the median of a data is 45.98 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use empirical formula)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The median of a data is 45.98 less than its mode.

**Formula used:**

Using the empirical formula: Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

**Calculation:**

Let Mode = M, Median = Me, Mean = μ

It is given that Median = Mode - 45.98

⇒ Me = M - 45.98

Using empirical formula:

M = 3(Me) - 2(μ)

Substitute Me = M - 45.98 into the formula:

⇒ M = 3(M - 45.98) - 2(μ)

⇒ M = 3M - 137.94 - 2(μ)

⇒ 2(μ) = 3M - M - 137.94

⇒ 2(μ) = 2M - 137.94

⇒ μ = M - 68.97

Now, Median exceeds Mean by:

⇒ Me - μ = (M - 45.98) - (M - 68.97)

⇒ Me - μ = -45.98 + 68.97

⇒ Me - μ = 22.99

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: If the median of a data is 80.32 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use empirical formula)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The median of the data is 80.32 less than its mode.

**Formula Used:**

Empirical formula: Mode = 3 × Median - 2 × Mean

**Calculation:**

Let Median = M, Mode = Mo, and Mean = Me.

Given: Median = Mode - 80.32

⇒ M = Mo - 80.32

Using the empirical formula: Mo = 3M - 2Me

Substitute Mo = M + 80.32 into the formula:

⇒ M + 80.32 = 3M - 2Me

⇒ 80.32 = 3M - M - 2Me

⇒ 80.32 = 2M - 2Me

Divide through by 2:

⇒ 40.16 = M - Me

The median exceeds the mean by 40.16.

**The correct answer is option 1: 40.16**

questions.question: If the median of a data is 71.24 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use the empirical formula)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The median of a dataset is 71.24 less than its mode.

**Formula used:**

Using the empirical formula:

Mode = 3 × Median - 2 × Mean

**Calculation:**

Let the median = M, mean = X, and mode = Mo.

Given: Mo = M + 71.24

Using the formula:

⇒ Mo = 3M - 2X

Substitute Mo = M + 71.24:

⇒ M + 71.24 = 3M - 2X

⇒ 71.24 = 3M - M - 2X

⇒ 71.24 = 2M - 2X

⇒ 71.24 = 2(M - X)

⇒ M - X = 35.62

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

f = Frequency of the median class
